findings.evidence: slugify_headings() now tracks fenced-code-block state via _FENCE_PATTERN and an in_fence toggle, skipping heading-pattern matching for any line between ``` or ~~~ delimiters. Verified against test_heading_like_line_inside_fenced_code_block_is_not_extracted (tests/test_anchors.py) and the end-to-end fixture test_fenced_code_block_content_produces_no_findings (tests/test_cli.py), both passing.
findings.fix: Fixed: fence-state tracking implemented in slugify_headings(), mirroring a real Markdown renderer's fenced-code-block exclusion.

findings.evidence: extract_links() now applies the same fence-state tracking as anchors.py, skipping link-pattern matching for any line between ``` or ~~~ delimiters. Verified against test_link_like_text_inside_fenced_code_block_is_not_extracted (tests/test_links.py) and the shared end-to-end fixture test_fenced_code_block_content_produces_no_findings (tests/test_cli.py), both passing.
findings.fix: Fixed: fence-state tracking implemented in extract_links(), consistent with the anchors.py exclusion (R-001).

findings.evidence: _check_anchor() now wraps target_file.read_text() in try/except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError), raising LinkAuditError(file=target_file, reason=str(exc)) instead of letting the raw exception propagate. Traced the call path: resolve_file() (called from cli._scan(), itself called inside cli.main()'s try block) lets this LinkAuditError bubble up uncaught to main()'s existing except LinkAuditError handler, which prints '{file}: {reason}' to stderr and returns exit 2 — the same contract used for the linking-file read. Verified against test_unreadable_anchor_target_raises_link_audit_error (tests/test_resolver.py) and test_unreadable_anchor_target_exits_2_and_names_file (tests/test_cli.py), both passing.
findings.fix: Fixed: the anchor-target read is now guarded identically to the linking-file read, routing through the existing exit-2 / actionable-error contract (Constitution Principles II and IV).

findings.evidence: resolve_file() now explicitly branches on parsed.file_part.startswith('/'): a root-relative target joins against root.lstrip-adjusted path (root / parsed.file_part.lstrip('/')) instead of base_dir / parsed.file_part, which previously let pathlib's absolute-path-overrides-join semantics silently resolve against the OS filesystem root. The non-root-relative branch (base_dir / parsed.file_part) is unchanged, confirming no regression to FR-004's base_dir-relative resolution. Verified against test_root_relative_link_resolves_against_repository_root, test_root_relative_link_to_missing_file_is_reported (tests/test_resolver.py), and test_root_relative_link_end_to_end (tests/test_cli.py), all passing.
findings.fix: Fixed: root-relative targets now resolve against the repository root (FR-015), matching spec.md's Q7 resolution.
